correctness.rationale: The specified 6x6 Langevin drift has positive definite stiffness for p,q>0,x>=0, and a Hurwitz generator because terminal damping rules out undamped eigenmodes. Stationary covariance is the unique Lyapunov solution, and equilibrium linearity reduces the flux to T_L=1,T_R=0. Exact 21-unknown symmetric covariance elimination yields det M=-64 det(K) D and det M-det(M_44)=-256 det(K)(S+2), with positive D=2(S+2)^2(4S+3)/(S+1)+8(S+1)(x-x0)^2. Cramer then gives J/(T_L-T_R)=2(S+1)(S+2)/((S+2)^2(4S+3)+4(S+1)^2(x-x0)^2), S=(p+q)/2+((p-q)/2)^2 and x0=(p+q)/2-3/2+1/(2(S+1)). Strict positive denominator coefficient implies the unique x>=0 maximum at max(0,x0). Differentiating x0 with respect to squared terminal contrast gives -1/[2(S+1)^2], and p=q onset (1+sqrt17)/4 is exact. Independent fresh covariance solves corroborate the eliminant; the universal proof is the polynomial identities plus quadratic geometry.
